question_text: How much electricity did your business consume in the last 12 months?
help_text: Check your electricity bills or smart meter readings. Include all premises your business operates from. Your energy supplier can provide an annual summary.
bank_relevance: Key input for Scope 2 GHG emissions calculation and energy efficiency assessment

question_text: What percentage of your energy comes from renewable sources?
help_text: Include on-site generation (solar panels, wind) and green energy tariffs from your supplier. If you don't use any renewables, answer 0%.
bank_relevance: Indicates transition risk profile and green loan eligibility under EU Taxonomy

question_text: How much fuel did your business use last year (gas, diesel, petrol, heating oil)?
help_text: Include fuel for heating/cooling your buildings and any owned or leased vehicles. Check utility bills and fuel card statements. You can give the total or break it down by type.
bank_relevance: Required to calculate Scope 1 direct GHG emissions for climate risk assessment

question_text: What were your total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions last year?
help_text: If you have a carbon footprint report or sustainability report, upload it here. If you haven't measured this, answer in your own words and Atlas will estimate from your energy data.
bank_relevance: Central metric for climate risk scoring, green loan covenants, and ECB stress tests

question_text: How much water does your business consume per year?
help_text: Check your water utility bills. Especially important for manufacturing, food & beverage, agriculture, hospitality, and healthcare sectors.
bank_relevance: Physical climate risk exposure; water stress in supply chain regions is a key credit risk factor

question_text: What percentage of your business waste is recycled, reused, or composted?
help_text: Estimate based on your waste collections. Your waste contractor may provide a certificate showing your recycling rate. If you have no data, give your best estimate.

value_schema.label: Percentage of total waste recycled or reused

bank_relevance: Circular economy alignment indicator; relevant for EU Taxonomy and green finance eligibility

question_text: How many people work at your company (full-time equivalent)?
help_text: Count all employees and regular contractors. Part-time staff count as a fraction (e.g., 3 days/week = 0.6 FTE). Include all locations.
bank_relevance: Baseline workforce metric; used to normalise per-employee emissions, safety rates, and productivity

question_text: What percentage of your workforce identifies as female?
help_text: Count all employees including part-time. This is required for gender diversity reporting under SFDR and many green lending frameworks.
bank_relevance: Social diversity metric required by SFDR PAI indicators and most green loan frameworks

question_text: Do all your permanent employees earn at or above the national minimum wage?
help_text: Confirm whether all workers (including part-time and temporary staff) receive at least the statutory minimum wage in their country.
bank_relevance: Social risk flag; non-compliance increases reputational and regulatory exposure for the lender

question_text: How many workplace injuries or accidents requiring medical attention occurred last year?
help_text: Include all incidents reported under your country's health & safety reporting rules. Zero is a valid and common answer. Your HR or EHS team will have this record.
bank_relevance: Operational risk indicator; high incident rates may signal management quality issues

question_text: Does your business have a written code of conduct or ethics policy?
help_text: This is a document setting out expected ethical behaviour, covering anti-bribery, conflicts of interest, whistleblowing, etc. Upload it here or describe what you have.
bank_relevance: Governance quality indicator; required for EU Green Bond Standard alignment and many sustainable finance products

question_text: Does your business have a formal environmental policy or management system?
help_text: Upload any policy document, ISO 14001 certificate, EMAS registration, or even a one-page environmental commitment. Having something written down is what matters.
bank_relevance: Demonstrates environmental management commitment; required for EU Taxonomy alignment claims

question_text: Do you have sustainability or ethics requirements for your key suppliers?
help_text: This could be a supplier code of conduct, a questionnaire you send them, or contractual clauses about environmental standards or labour practices.
bank_relevance: Value chain risk management; banks increasingly required to assess Scope 3 and supply chain exposure

question_text: Has your business identified any climate-related risks to its operations or premises?
help_text: For example: flood risk at your premises, extreme heat affecting staff or equipment, drought affecting your supply chain, or extreme weather disrupting logistics.
bank_relevance: Physical and transition risk disclosure required under Basel IV, ECB climate stress tests, and TCFD

question_text: Does your business hold any environmental, quality, or sustainability certifications?
help_text: Examples: ISO 14001 (environment), ISO 50001 (energy), ISO 9001 (quality), B Corp certification, EMAS, LEED, or sector-specific green certifications. Upload certificates if you have them.
bank_relevance: Third-party verified claims reduce due diligence burden and improve ESG credit scoring
